claims.claim_text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a cost-effective approach to improving large language model output so it remains relevant, accurate, and useful in various contexts.
claims.evidence_span: It is a cost-effective approach to improving LLM output so it remains relevant, accurate, and useful in various contexts.

claims.claim_text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation redirects the large language model to retrieve relevant information from authoritative, pre-determined knowledge sources.
claims.evidence_span: RAG is one approach to solving some of these challenges.

claims.claim_text: The difference between RAG and fine-tuning is that RAG lets an LLM query an external data source while fine-tuning trains an LLM on domain-specific data.
claims.evidence_span: The difference between RAG and fine-tuning is that RAG lets an LLM query an external data source while fine-tuning trains an LLM on domain-specific data.

claims.claim_text: Fine-tuning increases a model’s familiarity with the intended domain and output requirements, while RAG assists the model in generating relevant, high-quality outputs.
claims.evidence_span: Fine-tuning increases a model’s familiarity with the intended domain and output requirements, while RAG assists the model in generating relevant, high-quality outputs.

claims.claim_text: Once retrieved, the relevant information undergoes pre-processing, including tokenization, stemming, and removal of stop words.
claims.evidence_span: Once retrieved, the relevant information undergoes pre-processing, including tokenization, stemming, and removal of stop words.

claims.claim_text: This integration enhances the LLM's context, providing it with a more comprehensive understanding of the topic.
claims.evidence_span: This integration enhances the LLM's context, providing it with a more comprehensive understanding of the topic.

claims.claim_text: The term retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) was introduced in a 2020 paper that described combining a parametric language model with a non-parametric external memory accessed through retrieval at inference time.
claims.evidence_span: The term retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) was introduced in a 2020 paper that described combining a parametric language model with a non-parametric external memory accessed through retrieval at inference time.

claims.claim_text: Clock Tower X used RAG poisoning to flood the information space with sites and content sympathetic to Israel.
claims.evidence_span: Clock Tower X used RAG poisoning to flood the information space with sites and content sympathetic to Israel.

claims.claim_text: Developers can implement the retrieval-augmented generation process with as few as five lines of code.
claims.evidence_span: A blog by Lewis and three of the paper’s coauthors said developers can implement the process with as few as five lines of code.

claims.claim_text: Patrick Lewis led the author team of the 2020 paper that coined the term retrieval-augmented generation.
claims.evidence_span: Patrick Lewis, lead author of the 2020 paper that coined the term, apologized for the unflattering acronym that now describes a growing family of methods across hundreds of papers and dozens of commercial services he believes represent the future of generative AI.
